newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch- May 16.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch- May 16.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Friday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** Indian Prime Minister I.K. Gujral, meets the finance and petroleum ministers on Thursday on measures to plug a mounting oil subsidy bill, officials say
The United News of India (UNI) says the meeting took no decision on steps to contain the deficit. Further discussions would be held on the issue before arriving at a decision

** Analysts lower net profit forecasts scooter and motorcycle maker Bajaj Auto for the year ending March 31, 1998 by seven to 12 percent to 5.0 billion-5.3 billion rupees after the firm released its 1996/97 results on Wednesday
Bajaj Auto -- among the world's largest makers of two- and three-wheelers -- announced a modest five percent rise in net profit to 4.40 billion rupees, from 4.18 billion in 1995/96
The firm is due to meet for a bonus issue on May 19
** Shares of tobacco firm ITC Ltd are in the limelight ahead of its 1996/97 results on May 20. An earnings announcement is due on Saturday from pharmaceutical firm Dr Reddy's Laboratories
** State-owned foreign carrier Air India says it expects to earn a net profit of 912.6 million rupees ($25.49 million) in the financial year 1997/98 (April-March)
"We are basing our profit numbers on our achievements in the first quarter of calendar 1997," Brijesh Kumar, Managing Director of Air India told reporters in the Indian capital
** Finance Minister P. Chidambaram says foreign institutional investors invested $2.39 billion in 1996/97 (April-March) in India compared with $2.04 billion in the previous year
** Zee Telefilms says its 1996/97 net rises to 288.17 million rupees, from 230.27 million
** Private sector IndusInd Bank will make a public issue of equity in August-September this year, a bank official says

"The size of the issue is likely to be 450 million rupees. The premium will depend on how many times the earnings per share should be discounted," S. Solomon Raj, managing director of the bank, told Reuters
** Sugar firm Balarampur Chini says its 1996/97 net climbs to 236 million rupees, from 195.3 million in the previous year

** Department of Telecommunications (DoT) withdraws tariff hike for fixed to cellular mobile telephones. In its order, DoT says since the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) had quashed the tariff hike, application of this tariff would cease to exist with retrospective effect from May 1, 1997, Financial Express newspaper says
MARKETS:
** Bombay's benchmark share index .BSESN gains 0.69 pts to close at 3741.22 on Thursday -- off its intra-day high of 3767.21
** The National Stock Exchange index .NSEI edged up 3.35 points to 1,045.0 and the Madras index 11.91 points to 3,586.99.
-- Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
